Consider a conversation about what to have for dinner. Is coming to an agreement easier with two people or three? Three people or five? Five people or fifty? The higher the number, the more each individual's desires are averaged out to the least common denominator.

Now consider lobbying. I know, ancaps may tend to get hissy at the suggestion of DROs being lobbied, but they obviously would in the real world where influence is valuable. Especially influence upon the group that is protecting you. If the number of protectors goes up, that means there are more entities to lobby. More entities to lobby means you will be less successful in seeing your desires fulfilled. Considering these entities deal in protection, these desires are often the retention of property that exists under their domain, under their sphere of protection. And as the number of people to pander to increases, you will be less successful as your desires are balanced against the aggregate societal desires.

If the map of the world is more of a checkerboard, and even if those squares overlap, the people residing on one square are less and less likely to get their way in an adjacent square. If I own property in more than my immediate neighborhood, if I own property hundreds or thousands of miles away, it becomes increasingly difficult to influence the increasing number of relevant protection agencies to enforce that claim.

Thus, in a more polycentric world, the scale of modern western absentee ownership cannot be expected to be sustainable. Something's got to give, and if the equilibrium of protection agencies is stable it's not going to be them. It's going to be the far reaching claims to ownership that are no longer economically prudent to enforce or to lobby to have enforced.

If this is at all puzzling, it can be considered very analogous to the problem of rational ignorance in democracy. The more voters there are, the less each vote counts, and the less each voter cares to be informed. In this case the problem is not being informed, it is working to have your claims enforced. And as the number of protectors goes up, it is less and less sensible to pursue those claims the more distant they are, and conversely it is more and more sensible to only pursue the claims immediately around you. The scale of absentee ownership can be expected to shrink.
A hidden premise of ancap most of us don't want: reduce absentee ownership

If you can defend land, you own it. If you can't, you don't.

Later on, DROs will allow people to live in one place, and defend another place.

Even later still, courts will be able to dissuade some DROs from defending the "illegitimate" (according to the community in question) property.

It depends on how you look at it, absentee ownership to me is an externality enforced via taxes. I own property that I effectively abandoned however the state will continue to enforce my claim on it. The state's enforcement is funded via taxes which is the externality. Instead of me footing the bill for said enforcement burden fall on the taxpayers.

I think it's a relatively easy problem to solve if I actually care about the property. Pay the local DRO to protect my property when I am not there. Let's say I buy a beach house far away from my primary residence. I am at my beach house for maybe 15 days out of the year. If I don't want squatters to move in during the other 340 days I pay the local DRO or maybe a Home Owner's Association to make sure this doesn't happen. I imagine this will work same way for most property not just houses.

Hello, as the title tells I'm about to start Knights of the Old Republic, and when starting a new big game like this I always like to try to get some starter tips. If there are any tips for a new player Id love to know.
About to start playing Knights of the Old Republic for PC

Stay as low as a level as you possibly can until you become a Jedi. The amount of force powers you get during the game depends on how low your level is when you begin training, so if you're 3 levels lower than if you grinded them pre-jedi you'll have three extra powers when you hit max level.

Also, easy mode is really medium mode. Normal mode is hard mode. RNG sucks, so don't be afraid to go easy.
There are bugs in the console versions about this, so OP may have to take a level or two depending on the patching of the PC version.

On your first run you may find it very difficult to do this. Just try to stop at level 8 pre-Jedi; this gives you 12 levels in your Jedi class which ensures you get all the class feats.

If you decide to do a 2nd run then you can try to aim for level 5 (or less if you’re crazy).

StrategyWiki has tons of info on this and other aspects of KotOR gameplay.
How would I go about limiting my levels? Im scared to go to the wiki incase of possible spoilers.

Basically, levelling up is a manual process. After you receive enough experience to level, you have to click a button in your character sheet and then assign any talents/stats you receive for that level. Just ignore the level up button once you hit 8 (or 5, or whatever you choose).
